articles.title: Periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary hip arthroplasty : should the choice of femoral component design and fixation method vary according to the sex and age of the patient?
articles.authors: Borsheim S, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, Gjertsen JE, Furnes O, Dybvik E, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture by femoral component type, sex and age
articles.take_home: Cemented composite beam components had the lowest risk of femoral fractures around the implant compared with other designs, particularly in men over 75 and women over 70. Polished taper-slip components carried a high fracture risk in men of all ages.

articles.title: Barriers to recruitment in paediatric orthopaedic surgical trials : a qualitative study embedded in the Big BOSS trial.
articles.authors: Kirton JA, Achten J, Young B, Perry DC, Cherry MG
articles.study_type: Qualitative study embedded in a randomized controlled trial
articles.population: Consultant surgeons from NHS sites involved in the Big BOSS trial
articles.outcomes: Barriers to recruitment identified through thematic analysis of surgeon interviews
articles.take_home: The study found that recruitment to the Big BOSS trial was hindered by multiple factors including shortage of eligible patients, unclear eligibility criteria, surgeons' treatment preferences, limited research resources, and patients' concerns about surgery. Understanding these barriers can help improve how future surgical trials are designed and managed.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum in patients aged 50 years or older with hip dysplasia : a propensity score-matched comparative study.
articles.authors: Fujii M, Mochizuki H, Tanaka S, Kawano S, Ueno M, Oba Y, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 50 years or older with hip dysplasia undergoing transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum
articles.sample_size: 131 patients aged 50 years or older matched 1:1 with 131 patients aged under 50 years
articles.outcomes: Modified Harris Hip Score, joint survival at 10 and 20 years, patient-reported outcome measures, failure defined as progression to severe osteoarthritis or conversion to hip replacement, complications
articles.take_home: Transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum in patients aged 50 years or older achieved similar hip function improvements and long-term joint survival compared with younger patients, though those aged under 45 had better scores for sport and recreation and fewer complications. More advanced arthritis before surgery predicted a higher risk of eventual failure.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life following periprosthetic femoral fracture after total hip arthroplasty : a propensity score-matched cohort study with trajectory analysis.
articles.authors: Ablett AD, Powell-Bowns MFR, Super JT, Neo C, Yapp LZ, Clement ND, et al.
articles.study_type: Single-centre retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients who had a periprosthetic femoral fracture after total hip replacement, compared with general population controls
articles.sample_size: 140 patients with periprosthetic fracture matched with 700 general population controls; 22 patients with complete prospective data
articles.outcomes: Health-related quality of life measured by EQ-5D-3L, EQ-VAS, and Oxford Hip Score at median 2.9 years after fracture
articles.take_home: About two-thirds of patients had noticeably worse quality of life scores after a periprosthetic femoral fracture compared to the general population, with one in ten reporting health states worse than death. The fracture erased roughly one-third to two-fifths of the quality of life improvements that patients had gained from their hip replacement.

articles.title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Mohammad HR, Rahman A, Muhammad IM, Gill SS, Selim A, Thomas G, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Venous thromboembolism risk, deep vein thrombosis risk, bleeding risk, reoperation risk, and mortality
articles.take_home: Direct oral anticoagulants reduced the risk of blood clots after hip replacement compared with low molecular weight heparin injections, without increasing bleeding risk when using UK-approved doses. This could save the NHS £8.6 million per year.

articles.title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease.
articles.authors: Downie S, Kennedy M, Farhan-Alanie OM, Kennedy IW, McKean G, Kelly MP, et al.
articles.population: Patients with metastatic bone disease involving the hip undergoing femoral reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Reintervention for femoral implant failure was the primary outcome. Two-year probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025). Overall complication rate requiring further surgery was 8% (16 out of 205), with three reinterventions for femoral implant failure, all periprosthetic femoral fractures. No patients required femoral revision for loosening.
articles.take_home: A long uncemented hip implant that extends down the entire femur showed very low rates of failure or loosening in patients with metastatic cancer affecting the hip bone. The implant appears to be a safe and durable option for these patients, with only 1.5% needing revision surgery for implant failure.

articles.title: Hip-related tenotomy and progression to severe displacement of the hip in nonambulant children with cerebral palsy : a nationwide cohort study.
articles.authors: Bakhtiyar M, Iljazi A, Wong C, Petersen MM, Balslev-Clausen A
articles.population: Nonambulant children with cerebral palsy (GMFCS level IV or V) with established hip displacement
articles.sample_size: 259 children contributing 406 hips, of which 110 underwent tenotomy
articles.outcomes: Severe hip outcome defined as hip migration percentage of 50% or greater, or hip osteotomy surgery, followed up to ten years
articles.take_home: Children who had a hip-related tenotomy were less likely to develop severe hip problems over ten years compared to those who did not have the procedure, particularly those with less severe movement limitations. However, in children with the most severe movement limitations, progression of hip problems remained common regardless of surgery.

articles.title: Total hip arthroplasty improves global sagittal and coronal spinal imbalance and spinopelvic mobility : a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Leung TKC, Chan PK, Cheung A, Luk MH, Lau LCM, Cheung WK, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement for end-stage osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 163 patients (62 male, 101 female; mean age 68 years)
articles.outcomes: Change in sagittal vertical axis, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, proximal femoral angle, coronal balance parameters including limb length discrepancy and pelvic obliquity
articles.take_home: Hip replacement surgery improved spinal balance in patients who had imbalance before surgery, correcting limb length differences and allowing better hip and pelvic movement. About one in four patients with poor sagittal balance and one in three with poor coronal balance moved into the balanced group after surgery.

articles.title: Three working windows posterior midline approach for posterior column tibial plateau fractures.
articles.authors: Wang X, Zhang S, Yan J, Jiang D, Shi C, Yin Z, et al.
articles.population: Patients with isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression
articles.outcomes: Joint reduction and alignment, fracture union time, knee flexion and extension range, HSS knee score, wound complications, neurovascular injuries
articles.take_home: A surgical approach using three working windows from a single posterior incision successfully treated these complex knee fractures in all 10 patients, with good bone healing and knee movement restored, though two patients had manageable complications.

articles.title: Rethinking early arthrogenic muscle inhibition after total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Qu X, Sun G, Chen B
articles.population: Patients after total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Arthrogenic muscle inhibition at 30 and 60 days post-operatively
articles.take_home: Early muscle inhibition around the knee at 30 days after knee replacement surgery predicts whether it will persist at 60 days, but this does not necessarily mean the early inhibition is the main cause of later problems. The study identifies a useful pattern to watch for but does not fully explain why the muscle weakness continues.

articles.title: Optimising methodology, biomechanics and imaging in biological augmentation for partial-thickness rotator cuff tears: A commentary on Demiral et al.
articles.authors: He H, Shen W, Tao J
articles.population: Patients with partial-thickness rotator cuff tears
articles.outcomes: Clinical and radiological improvements; tear volume estimation on MRI
articles.take_home: This commentary examines how to improve research on platelet-rich plasma combined with physical therapy for partial rotator cuff tears, highlighting the need for better study design, clearer rehabilitation guidance, and more precise imaging measurements.

articles.title: Restricted Kinematic Alignment Improves Function, But Does Not Reduce Kinesiophobia After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A 3-Year Follow-Up Study.
articles.authors: Chen Z, Xiao M, Luo F, Luo J, Chen L, Xu J
articles.study_type: Secondary analysis of a prospective randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Kinesiophobia measured by Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia-11; functional outcomes measured by Oxford Knee Score and Forgotten Joint Score at multiple time points over 3 years
articles.take_home: Restricted kinematic alignment improved knee function slightly compared to mechanical alignment, but neither approach reduced fear of movement after surgery. Reducing fear of movement was linked to better function regardless of which surgical technique was used.

articles.title: Optimizing Intraoperative Tissue Sampling in Hip and Knee Periprosthetic Joint Infection: Deep Bone Provides Higher Culture Yield in One-Stage Exchange.
articles.authors: Russo A, Zanna L, Luo TD, Gehrke T, Citak M
articles.population: Patients undergoing one-stage exchange surgery for periprosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Culture positivity rates by intraoperative sampling location (deep bone, superficial bone, soft tissue)
articles.take_home: Taking samples from deep bone during surgery to treat hip or knee infections around joint replacements is more likely to identify the infection-causing bacteria compared to samples from superficial bone or soft tissue. Samples from soft tissue worked particularly well for hip infections.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Fascia Iliaca Compartment Block Combined with Two Different Patient-Controlled Analgesia Regimens for Hip Arthroplasty: A Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Li M, Li Y, Zhou Y, Qin Z
articles.study_type: Retrospective observational study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing unilateral hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative pain scores (VAS) at 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours; adverse events; opioid consumption; hospital stay length; complications
articles.take_home: Patients who received a nerve block combined with continuous nerve block pain relief had better pain control after hip surgery and needed less opioid medication than those who received standard intravenous pain relief, with similar safety and recovery.

articles.title: From Innovation to Accountability: Ethical Standards for Orthopaedic Implant Safety.
articles.authors: Iorio R, Sabet C, Ottesen T, Franco JR, Bosco J 3rd, Mercuri JJ, et al.
articles.outcomes: Framework for decision-making on when to pause new implantation, notify patients, suspend use, or recall orthopaedic implants
articles.take_home: The study proposes a clearer system for responding to safety problems with orthopaedic implants, suggesting that stopping new implants should happen sooner than revising ones already in place, and that decisions should be transparent and made before widespread harm occurs.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Patient-Facing Total Knee Arthroplasty Information in Knee Osteoarthritis: Development and Application of the Composite Clinical Reliability Score.
articles.authors: Muthu S, Kolarpatti Ponnusamy DV, Rathinam MM, Viswanathan VK, Rajappan Chandra SK, Sharun K
articles.study_type: Comparative evaluation study of large language models
articles.population: Patient-facing information about total knee arthroplasty for knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 90 patient questions generating 270 responses from three large language models, assessed by two orthopaedic surgeons
articles.outcomes: Composite Clinical Reliability Score across six domains (factual accuracy, clinical correctness, guideline adherence, hallucination severity, clinical safety, evidence citation validity) and readability assessment
articles.take_home: One large language model (Program 2) performed better overall at providing reliable, safe and readable information about knee replacement surgery, though all three models had different strengths and weaknesses. Large language models should only be used to supplement, not replace, advice from healthcare professionals.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Re-Revision After Aseptic Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: Knees Revised for Instability Re-Fail Early in a Single-Center Cohort With a Mean 14-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Chen PY, Lau NC, Peng SH, Lee SH, Chang Y, Lin YC
articles.population: Patients undergoing aseptic revision total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Survivorship free of re-revision at 10 and 15 years; risk factors for re-revision; functional scores (Knee Society and Oxford Knee scores); failure modes
articles.take_home: Aseptic revision knee replacements are durable with over 80% surviving 15 years without needing further revision surgery. Knees revised because of instability are most likely to fail early (within 3 years), and those with prior revision surgery or severe bone loss also have higher re-revision risk.

articles.title: Delayed return to sport after fat pad debridement: A surgical effect or a load-tolerance signal?
articles.authors: Han X, Yang M
articles.population: Patients with chronic patellar tendinopathy undergoing surgery
articles.outcomes: Return to sport time after fat pad debridement versus other surgical interventions
articles.take_home: Fat pad debridement may be a marker of more irritable knee pain rather than causing delayed return to sport, and timing of return alone does not guarantee full recovery without proper rebuilding of tendon strength. Future studies need better tracking of fat pad status and individualised rehabilitation plans to understand whether preserving the fat pad actually helps athletes recover faster.

articles.title: Arthroscopic labral repair versus debridement in non-athletic patients with femoroacetabular impingement: A prospective randomized study.
articles.authors: Salem KA, Elsaeed AM, Ganzouri IE, Abdelrahman AA, Abdelwahab MM, Hemida MA
articles.population: Non-athletic patients with femoroacetabular impingement (mean age 32.1 years)
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score, Hip Outcome Score-Activities of Daily Living, and Visual Analogue Scale pain scores at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: Labral repair produced better function and pain relief in the first 3 to 6 months after surgery compared to debridement, but by 12 months the two treatments had similar results. Repair took longer to perform but had similar complication rates.

articles.title: Rethinking the functional relevance of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures in anterior cruciate ligament injury.
articles.authors: Qu X, Tang X, Yang D, Chen B
articles.population: Patients with anterior cruciate ligament injury and posterolateral tibial plateau fractures
articles.outcomes: Association between posterolateral tibial plateau fractures and lateral-sided soft-tissue pathology; preoperative pivot shift laxity
articles.take_home: The presence of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures alone may not reliably predict how unstable the knee will feel, as the significance depends on the size and depth of the fracture, which varies considerably between patients. More research is needed to understand how severe fracture types affect knee function.

articles.title: Association between cemented and uncemented cups and risk of revision in patients aged 65 years or older following primary total hip arthroplasty: a study of 310,515 patients from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association.
articles.authors: Latifi R, Kornvig S, Mohaddes M, Ali M, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years or older undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for primary osteoarthritis or sequelae of childhood hip disorders
articles.outcomes: All-cause cup revision rates comparing cemented and uncemented acetabular cups, stratified by age and sex, with follow-up divided into three periods: 0-1 year, 1-6 years, and 6-26 years
articles.take_home: Cemented cups had a lower revision risk in the first year after surgery across all older patients, but a higher revision risk from 6 to 26 years later. In patients aged 80 and over, there was no clear difference between cemented and uncemented cups after the first year.

articles.title: Mental Health Must Become Central in Periprosthetic Joint Infection Care.
articles.authors: Higuera-Rueda CA, Lizcano JD, Shehadeh TH, Villa JM, Hernandez V, Jimenez D, et al.
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Mental health burden, quality of life, depression, anxiety, social isolation, psychological distress
articles.take_home: Current treatment of joint infections after joint replacement focuses on clearing the infection but largely ignores mental health problems like depression and anxiety that affect many patients. The authors argue that mental health screening and support should become a standard part of treatment to improve how patients actually feel and recover.

articles.title: Sports After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Cross-Sectional Web-Based Study Among Members of the Brazilian Hip Society.
articles.authors: Freitas A, Diesel CV, Busato TS, Miranda RH, Nunes Pires OG, Giordano MN
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons who are full members of the Brazilian Hip Society
articles.outcomes: Consensus-based recommendations on which sports are permitted after total hip replacement and optimal timing for resuming activities
articles.take_home: Most sports were considered safe to resume after hip replacement, typically starting around 12 weeks after surgery, though high-impact and contact sports need caution. These recommendations come from what surgeons think is best rather than what patients actually experienced.

articles.title: Prospective Evaluation of an Intraoperative Synovial Calprotectin Point-of-Care Lateral Flow Test for Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Hip and Knee Revisions.
articles.authors: Giatroudakis K, Iliopoulos E, Kateros K, Giannikas K, Patsiogiannis N, Oikonomou L, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision hip or knee replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of a point-of-care calprotectin test for detecting joint infection using a threshold of 50 mg/L
articles.take_home: A new rapid test measuring calprotectin in joint fluid during revision surgery was highly accurate at detecting infection in both hip and knee replacements, correctly identifying infection in over 87% of infected cases and ruling it out in over 90% of non-infected cases. The test provides results quickly during surgery to help surgeons make immediate treatment decisions.

articles.title: The 10-Year Revision Risk of Dual-Mobility Versus Standard Cups in Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty for Osteoarthritis: A Population-Based Study from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Hussein Y, Iljazi A, Sorensen MS, Eriksson F, Overgaard S, Petersen MM
articles.study_type: Population-based cohort study using national register data
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis between 2007 and 2019
articles.sample_size: 56,051 patients (5,187 with dual-mobility cups, 35,162 with standard 36mm cups, 15,702 with standard 32mm cups)
articles.outcomes: 10-year revision risk for any cause and cause-specific revision (dislocation and infection)
articles.take_home: Dual-mobility cups and standard cups had similar overall revision rates at 10 years. Dual-mobility cups reduced dislocation revisions but were associated with higher infection-related revisions compared to standard cups.

articles.title: Effect of Horizontal Medialization of the Hip Center of Rotation on Clinical Outcomes After Total Hip Arthroplasty in Crowe Types I and II Developmental Hip Dysplasia.
articles.authors: Duan Z, Huang X, Zhang Y, Huang H, Ma M, Tian C, et al.
articles.population: Patients with Crowe types I and II developmental dysplasia of the hip undergoing total hip replacement
articles.sample_size: 189 patients (108 in reconstruction group, 81 in medialization group)
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score, Oxford Hip Score, pain scores, limping, radiographic parameters, and complications including dislocation
articles.take_home: Moving the hip centre of rotation inwards during hip replacement surgery for mild to moderate developmental dysplasia did not lead to worse pain, function, or walking compared to normal positioning. This suggests that some inward movement of the hip centre is acceptable if the socket is properly positioned and stable.

articles.title: Low Artificial Intelligence-Estimated Bone Mineral Density From Chest Radiographs Is Associated With Delayed Pain Recovery and Lower Quality of Life After Medial Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Yamagami R, Moro T, Kono K, Kawaguchi K, Taketomi S, Tanaka S
articles.population: Patients undergoing cemented medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 336 procedures reviewed; 58 low bone mineral density matched with 58 controls
articles.outcomes: Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) subscales including pain and quality of life, measured preoperatively to three years postoperatively
articles.take_home: Patients with low bone mineral density had slower pain recovery in the first year after knee replacement surgery and reported lower quality of life scores up to three years after the operation. However, the implants remained stable and functioned similarly to those in patients with normal bone density.

articles.title: Short-term benefits of hybrid graft in medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction for recurrent patellar dislocation: A prospective randomized controlled trial with minimum 2-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Zhai W, Wang D, Xu S, Zhou H, Guo J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with recurrent patellar dislocation undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 46 patients (22 autograft, 24 hybrid graft); mean age 19.3 years, 82.6% female
articles.outcomes: Kujala and IKDC functional scores at 3, 6, 12 months and final follow-up; patellar lateral tilt angle and patellar-trochlear groove distance on imaging
articles.take_home: Hybrid graft reconstruction (combining tendon and artificial tape) helped patients recover knee function faster than autograft alone in the first 6 months, with both approaches achieving similar good results by 12 months and beyond.

articles.title: Contact injury mechanism is independently associated with greater Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Severity Scale severity in patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Malhame ZM, Hardy A, Bouche PA, Santoli A, Miele A, Seil R, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction after sport-related complete anterior cruciate ligament rupture
articles.outcomes: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Severity Scale severity grade and continuous score, assessed by magnetic resonance imaging and arthroscopy
articles.take_home: Injuries caused by contact (such as being tackled) were associated with more severe damage to the knee than non-contact injuries. The type of sport played did not independently affect injury severity once contact mechanism was accounted for.

articles.title: Double-level osteotomy versus high tibial osteotomy for varus malalignment of the knee: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Alkatheeri A, Ghandour M, Mobarak HA, Pierce T, Bonne S, Chalfoun AD, et al.
articles.population: Patients with varus knee malalignment undergoing surgery
articles.sample_size: 805 knees (306 double-level osteotomy, 499 high tibial osteotomy) from 9 observational studies
articles.outcomes: Joint-line obliquity, radiographic angles (MPTA, LDFA, mLDFA), patient-reported outcome scores (KOOS, KSS), return to sport, operative time, hinge fracture rate, nonunion rate
articles.take_home: At 3 years follow-up, both surgical techniques produced similar patient satisfaction and functional results. Double-level osteotomy achieved better radiographic alignment with fewer fractures during surgery, but took longer to perform.

articles.title: Stable 2-year migration on radiostereometric analysis and improved gait speed and function after bicruciate-retaining TKA: a prospective cohort of 25 patients.
articles.authors: Mills K, Van Laarhoven SN, Defoort KC, Susan S, Heesterbeek PJC
articles.population: Patients undergoing bicruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Component migration measured by radiostereometric analysis at 2 years; gait speed, stride length and stride time; patient-reported outcome measures; adverse events
articles.take_home: The knee replacement remained stable over 2 years with good fixation. Patients reported significant improvements in their symptoms and quality of life after surgery, though gains in walking speed were small.

articles.title: Arthroplasty versus internal fixation for displaced femoral neck fractures in older patients with dementia: a target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Jensen SS, Gundtoft PH, Nelissen RGHH, Gjertsen JE, Pedersen AB
articles.study_type: Comparative effectiveness study using target trial emulation with nationwide registry data
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and over with dementia and displaced femoral neck fracture
articles.sample_size: 3,161 patients (2,231 received arthroplasty, 930 received internal fixation)
articles.outcomes: Primary: reoperation within 365 days. Secondary: major reoperation, mortality, length of stay, early mobilisation, mobility decline
articles.take_home: Internal fixation was associated with fewer repeat operations and lower death rates than arthroplasty in older patients with dementia and hip fractures. However, the researchers noted that the study design cannot prove which treatment directly caused better outcomes, as other unmeasured differences between patients may have influenced the results.
